cards.explanation: The messenger is sent to prepare the way, friends. Mark quotes Isaiah the prophet: “Behold, I will send My messenger ahead of You, who will prepare Your way.” Think of it like a baker who sets out the bowls and heats the oven before the dough ever shows up. The messenger's work happens before the main event.

The answer is True, bakers. The voice is calling in the wilderness, “Prepare the way for the Lord, make straight paths for Him.” Those straight paths are right there in Mark 1:3. Mark is telling us the Lord is coming, and the way needs to be ready.

John is preaching a baptism for the forgiveness of sins, friends. Mark says John was “…preaching a baptism of repentance for the forgiveness of sins” (Mark 1:4). Repentance means turning from sin, and John's baptism went with that. That's the message he's shouting out in the wilderness.
The answer is False, bakers. Mark 1:5 says, “Confessing their sins, they were baptized by him in the Jordan River.” They confessed their sins, and they were baptized. So the people do confess.

John eats locusts and wild honey, friends. Mark 1:6 says, “His food was locusts and wild honey.” Locusts are insects, and the honey is wild. I've burned some batches in my day, but even my worst one beats that.

John says he is not worthy to untie the sandals of the One coming after him, bakers. In Mark 1:7 he says, “…the straps of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie.” People came out from all of Jerusalem and the countryside of Judea to see John (Mark 1:5), and he says he isn't even worthy for that small job. He knows who's coming after him.

The answer is water, friends. John says in Mark 1:8, “I baptize you with water…” And he does it in the Jordan River, as verse 5 says. Then he points ahead to One who will baptize with the Holy Spirit.
The answer is False, bakers. Mark 1:9 says Jesus “…was baptized by John in the Jordan.” He came from Nazareth in Galilee and went into the water. John doesn't turn Him away.

What Jesus sees descending on Him is the Spirit, friends. Mark 1:10 says He “…saw the heavens breaking open and the Spirit descending on Him like a dove.” The Spirit is what comes down, and it comes “…like a dove.” It's a gentle picture.

The answer is True, bakers. The voice from heaven says, “You are My beloved Son; in You I am well pleased.” Those words are for Jesus, and Mark records them (Mark 1:11). Beloved Son is exactly what the voice calls Him.
The word is wilderness, friends. Mark 1:12 says, “At once the Spirit drove Jesus into the wilderness…” It happens right after the baptism. Verse 13 then tells us what happens out there.
The number is forty, bakers! Mark 1:13 says, “…He was there for forty days, being tempted by Satan.” Forty days is a long stretch to be out there. And the verse says He wasn't there alone.
The angels take care of Him, friends. Mark 1:13 says, “…the angels ministered to Him.” To minister means to serve and care for. So even out there with the wild animals, the angels were with Jesus.
